subject: Annual token engagement structure for BrightRetail
messages:
From: Hannah Bright <hannah@brightretail.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Annual commit options and flexibility

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're sizing our roadmap for next year and need a simple annual commitment structure we can present to procurement. High level:
- ~50M tokens/year baseline with seasonal spikes up to 90M in Q4.
- Need clear overage terms and burst guarantees (esp. Black Friday window).
- Procurement asks for an option to phase payments quarterly and a clause for a single SOW amendment if usage materially exceeds the commit.

Can you share a realistic Starter/Growth/Enterprise breakdown with expected per-token pricing, overage rates, and any credits for unused commit? A one-page matrix would be ideal.

Oliver (cc) will own the numbers on our side — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Hannah Bright
Head of Product Ops
BrightRetail

Attachments: none
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Bright <hannah@brightretail.com>
Cc: Oliver Jensen <oliver.jensen@brightretail.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual commit options and flexibility

Hannah — thanks for the clear brief. Drafted a concise structure below that maps to typical BrightRetail usage patterns and gives you flexibility on ramping/payment. Attached is a starter one-pager (proposal-v1) — I'll follow up with a revised file after internal alignment.

Summary (annual commitments):
- Starter: 5M tokens/year — $0.00095 / token (no overage discount). Good for pilot teams and low-traffic features.
- Growth: 50M tokens/year — $0.00072 / token (8% effective discount vs list). Overage: $0.00095 / token; 20% of unused commit convertible to credits once annually.
- Enterprise: 150M tokens/year — $0.00058 / token (25% effective discount). Overage: $0.00065 / token; includes burst capacity (2x baseline) with 99.5% best-effort SLA during events; dedicated routing priority.

Key commercial notes:
- Ramp & payments: we can invoice quarterly; credits issued for sustained underutilization >30% for the year (subject to reconciliation).
- Overage smoothing: first 10% over commit billed at overage rate; above that we can provide a blended rate discussion or convert to a short-term buffer commitment.
- Burst windows: for guaranteed burst during Black Friday we recommend an add-on short-term reserved capacity block — pricing depends on forecasted peak TPS; otherwise Enterprise includes soft-priority burst.
- Term: 12 months with 30-day notice for changes to scope.

Next steps: 1) I'll loop in Rishi to validate the cost/tech optimizations that justify the Growth vs Enterprise numbers, 2) we can set a call to finalize ramp schedule and legal checklist.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Annual commit options and flexibility — usage & optimization notes

Forwarding with a quick technical/ops note to align pricing to realistic production economics. See attached forecast.

Key points to consider when choosing between Growth and Enterprise: 
- Effective tokens consumed can be reduced by 20–40% depending on prompt design, caching, and response-length control. Recommend a quick eval on 10 representative prompts (we can run sample evals).
- Batching & prefix caching: for BrightRetail search suggestions, prefix caching will cut repeated token generation during sessions; this favors a Growth commit with 8% discount vs paying higher Enterprise prices.
- Quantization & model choice: Enterprise commit assumes a higher-performance quantized runtime (faster latencies) — helps during Q4 peak but increases the commit threshold because we reserve capacity.
- Overage handling: implement a passive overage alert + automated fallback to a compatible cheaper model variant before billing hits the overage slab.

Attached: usage-forecast.csv (monthly forecast sample), tech-ops-notes.md (short checklist).

Happy to run a 30-min workshop with Oliver to map forecast to tiers.

—Rishi
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Bright <hannah@brightretail.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Jensen <oliver.jensen@brightretail.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual commit options and flexibility

Thanks, Kimberly and Rishi — useful detail. A few negotiation items from procurement/finance: 

1) Overage rate: can you tighten Enterprise overage to $0.00055/token and remove the stepped blended conversation? We need a predictable cap for our CFO.
2) Burst guarantee: for Black Friday we'll likely need guaranteed capacity. Can you put a clause for a three-day reserved burst at a fixed fee (we'll supply a forecast by May 1)?
3) Credits: rather than converting unused commit to credits only once a year, can we do quarterly reconciliations and roll forward up to 15% unused credit?

Oliver and I prefer quarterly invoicing and a kickoff SOW that includes an initial 30-day ramp assessment. If you can accept (1) and (3) above, procurement is likely to sign.

On timing — can we target final T&Cs by end of next week and legal review the week after?

Best,
Hannah
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Bright <hannah@brightretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual token engagement structure for BrightRetail — revised proposal

Hannah / Oliver — appreciate the clear asks. I've updated the commercial terms to reflect the points you raised and attached the revised proposal (brightretail-proposal-v2.pdf) for procurement review. Summary of changes: 

- Enterprise overage: reduced to $0.00055/token for the first 20% over commit; beyond that we revert to the previously shared overage rate. This gives your CFO a predictable cap in most plausible scenarios.
- Burst guarantee: we can offer a 3-day reserved burst block (one-time fee TBD) — schedule and exact TPS/GB needs required by May 1 to lock pricing.
- Credits & reconciliation: quarterly reconciliation accepted; up to 15% of unused commit can be rolled forward into the next quarter as credit. Annual true-up still applies at contract end.
- Payments: quarterly invoicing confirmed. SOW: initial 30-day ramp assessment clause added.

I've added HubSpot deal BR-2027-005 to the proposal and included a link to our shared Drive document and my Calendly for a final handoff call. If that looks good, I'll ask legal to issue a redline-friendly master agreement and we can target signatures the week after next.

Next actions:
- Oliver: confirm peak forecast for Black Friday by May 1 (aditya_rao@redwood.com will coordinate the capacity quote).
- Kimberly: schedule pricing handoff call (calendly link below).
- Rishi: prepare the short technical SOW annex for the 30-day ramp.

Thanks — excited to get BrightRetail onboarded.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
